page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Headpiece ornament above the heading (not text). Running head at top centre. Page number at top left. Heading "CAPVT VI." with a centred italic title below it. Catchword at bottom right.

main_text.p: vere actualiter & essentialiter monstruosissimum corpus ex tot corporum substantiis constatum, nasceretur, quot unquam fuerunt, sunt & erunt vera Christi membra, quod res ipsa clamat, & satis superque fuisse confido manifeste demonstratum. Nos autem e contrario sicut Sacramentalium signorum & rerum significatarum nexum ἐνεργητικὸν[?], & Sacramentalem esum ac potum, metonymice sic vocari ostedimus: sic huius unitionis & communionis modum mere tum suis partibus omnibus, tū suo fine, affirmamus non simpliciter intellectualem, sed plane spiritualem, divinum ac cœlestè esse, cuius τὸ ὅτι quidè, ex Dei verbo, tum simplici, tum Sacramentali, nobis patet, effectum vero, optimo iure, Apostolus magnum mysterium appellat. Utra vero sit vera, id est, capitibus nostræ religionis conueniēs sententia, & an non seipsas collidant ratio-nes ab iis allatæ, quibus eundem modum simul & corporalem, & invisibilem, & incomprehensibilem esse volunt, non recuso, quin ex contrario prolatis utrinque argumentis, ab i-doneis iudicibus dispiciatur.
main_text.head: CAPUT VI.

head.i: Responsio ad Physica eorum argumenta qui verum Christi corpus essentiale negant, nisi essentialiter in terris adsit, posse vere per fidem apprehensum credentibus communicari.

page.notes:
The Greek word after "nexum" is worn and printed unclearly; read as ἐνεργητικὸν with doubt. The title line is partly worn, and "vere per fidem" is read as printed. The catchword "Quis" is the final word of this page's text, set at the foot right; it is given as a catchword and also as a last

, which may be a duplication, so the

has been kept only for its printed position and may be removed if the catchword is taken alone. No marginal notes are printed on this page.
